title: US tariffs under section 122 and support for Singapore businesses
asked: MPs asked what clarifications Singapore is seeking from the US on the section 122 tariff, how US–Singapore FTA exports will be treated, when sector-specific guidance will be issued, what indicators would trigger extra support, and whether exemptions can be negotiated based on the US goods trade surplus.
asked_by: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Dr Choo Pei Ling
response: Ms Gan Siow Huang said the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariffs on 20 February 2026, and the US then announced a 10% section 122 tariff for 150 days, collected from 24 February 2026; President Trump announced a rise to 15% but no official directive had been issued. She said the immediate direct impact on Singapore is not expected to be significant because the 10% rate is broadly unchanged, though precision engineering and some general manufacturing segments could see greater impact. She cited SERT, BizAdapt support raised to up to 70% at Budget 2026, GRIT, and an SBF playbook, and said Singapore is deepening, diversifying and defending trade links and pursuing emerging markets and FTAs.

key_points.point: US Supreme Court struck down the US reciprocal tariffs on 20 February 2026.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: the Supreme Court of the United States struck down the US' "reciprocal" tariffs

key_points.point: US announced a 10% tariff under section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 on all US imports for 150 days.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: the US announced a tariff of 10% under section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 on all US imports for 150 days

key_points.point: US Customs and Border Protection started collecting the 10% tariff from 12.01 am on 24 February 2026, US time.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The US Customs and Border Protection started collecting this 10% tariff from 12.01 am on 24 February 2026, US time.

key_points.point: President Trump announced a rise to 15% via Truth Social on 21 February 2026, but the US has yet to issue an official directive.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: While US President Donald Trump announced via a Truth Social post on 21 February 2026 that the tariff rate would be raised to 15%, the US has yet to issue an official directive on this increase.

key_points.point: Immediate direct impact on Singapore's economy is not expected to be significant.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: The immediate direct impact of these tariff developments on Singapore's economy is not expected to be significant

key_points.point: Precision engineering and some segments under general manufacturing could see greater impact from any tariff increase.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: such as the precision engineering cluster and some segments under the general manufacturing cluster, could see a greater impact from any tariff increase

key_points.point: SERT convened last week to discuss tariff developments and preliminary sentiments of businesses and workers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: SERT convened last week to discuss the tariff developments and preliminary sentiments of businesses and workers.

key_points.point: BizAdapt was launched in October 2025 to help businesses evaluate impact, optimise supply chains and reconfigure operations.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: In October 2025, SERT launched the Business Adaptation Grant (BizAdapt) to help businesses affected by the tariffs to evaluate the impact, optimise their supply chains and reconfigure their operations.

key_points.point: Budget 2026 raised BizAdapt support levels from up to 50% to up to 70%.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: support levels under BizAdapt would be raised from up to 50%, to up to 70%.

key_points.point: SBF published a playbook on risk-mapping, reconfiguring supply chains, digitalising and innovating.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: SBF has published a playbook to guide companies on key actions to take, such as how to sense-make the impact through risk-mapping, to take action, such as re-configuring their supply chains, and also planning ahead by digitalising and innovating to build long-term resilience.

key_points.point: Singapore will deepen, diversify and defend its economic interest and trade linkages.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: Singapore will continue to safeguard and expand our economic space by deepening, diversifying and also defending our economic interest

key_points.point: Singapore is pursuing closer trade relations with emerging markets such as Latin America, South Asia, Middle East and Africa.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: we are also pursuing closer trade relations with emerging markets, such as Latin America, South Asia, Middle East and Africa

key_points.point: Businesses are encouraged to tap Singapore's 29 Free Trade Agreements, including CPTPP and RCEP.
key_points.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
key_points.quote: We encourage businesses to continue tapping on our 29 Free Trade Agreements, including the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.

left_open: Specific clarifications Singapore is seeking from the US on the scope, product coverage and customs implementation of the section 122 tariff.
How Singapore's exports under the US–Singapore Free Trade Agreement will be treated.
When sector-specific guidance for businesses, including re-exporters, will be issued.
Quantitative indicators or thresholds that would trigger additional support measures.
Whether any measures being studied will be sector-targeted.
Whether Singapore will negotiate exemptions based on the increasing US goods trade surplus with Singapore.
Assessment of the impact if the 15% tariff takes effect.
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on contingency planning for persistent or sector-specific tariffs and strengthening Singapore's trade resilience.
